research_question: What documentary evidence is necessary to substantiate that a named AI rack configuration at a named site has been installed, commissioned, accepted and operationally observed, and what can the present public record establish?

scope.technical: NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 racks and the DGX SuperPOD reference architecture, as already recorded in Evidence Release 006 and the IDE-006 dossier
scope.temporal: Sources dated 2024 to 2026; ten sources rechecked on 2026-11-12
scope.site: None. No site, operator, customer, contract or deployment is represented or implied
excluded: Statements about whether any particular site is in service

boundary: A research candidate, not an assessment of any site. It sets out which records could support which evidence state, and finds that the public record supports none of the site-level states. It records no human or scientific review, makes no engineering or legal determination and does not promote any Atlas relationship.

attributes.configuration_identity: Identifies the configuration: model, rack or cluster, and serial numbers where a physical unit is meant
attributes.dated: Carries the date of the act it records
attributes.issuing_party: Names the organisation that issued it
attributes.signatory_authority: Signed by a person able to bind the issuing party
attributes.method: States the procedure or test method used
attributes.criteria: States the pass or acceptance thresholds in advance
attributes.results: Records the observed results, not only a pass mark
attributes.conditions: States the operating and environmental conditions of the test
attributes.completeness: Covers every item it claims to cover, with exceptions listed

record_types.label: Vendor product specification or user guide
record_types.does_not_establish: That any unit was ordered, delivered, installed or operated anywhere

record_types.label: Vendor reference architecture
record_types.does_not_establish: That a site follows the design, or that the design was tested at the proposed scale

record_types.label: Vendor deployment, bring-up or operations procedure
record_types.does_not_establish: That the procedure was carried out, by whom or with what result

record_types.label: Published checklist with unchecked items
record_types.does_not_establish: That any item was checked, or that anyone signed or approved it

record_types.label: Vendor performance figure or validation-test description
record_types.does_not_establish: That any installed system reached the figure, or under what conditions

record_types.label: Site design for a named facility (single-line diagram, mechanical plan)
record_types.does_not_establish: That the design was built or energised

record_types.label: Contract, service or utility supply agreement for a named site
record_types.does_not_establish: That equipment was delivered or capacity was energised

record_types.label: Agreed acceptance criteria for a named configuration
Purchase order for named equipment
record_types.does_not_establish: That the equipment was delivered or installed

record_types.label: Delivery or receiving record with serial numbers
record_types.does_not_establish: That the equipment was installed or connected

record_types.label: Installation record: rack placement, power, coolant and network connection
record_types.does_not_establish: That any subsystem was energised or passed a test

record_types.label: Completed commissioning test for one subsystem, with results
Integrated test across subsystems under stated conditions
record_types.does_not_establish: That the parties accepted the configuration, or that it operated over time

record_types.label: Signed acceptance of a named configuration against agreed criteria
record_types.does_not_establish: That the configuration operated as accepted over any later period

record_types.label: Operational monitoring over a stated period
record_types.does_not_establish: That the workload performance claimed was achieved

record_types.label: Measured workload performance with method and conditions
record_types.does_not_establish: That the result generalises to other workloads or sites

record_types.label: Current regulatory text or announcement
record_types.does_not_establish: How any named item, party or transaction is treated

record_types.label: Licence, classification or determination for a named transaction
record_types.does_not_establish: That the facility is technically able to operate the system

chain.title: Specification and design
chain.question: What does the published configuration establish, and what does a design propose?

category_errors.inference: Treating a reference architecture as tested at the scale a site builds
category_errors.why_not: NVIDIA states tested scale for its own reference design only, and its wording on that scale is itself unresolved

category_errors.inference: Treating a product specification as describing any site
category_errors.why_not: A specification states what a product is; it names no site, configuration instance or date

chain.title: Procurement and delivery
chain.question: What shows that the configuration was contracted, ordered and delivered to a named site?

category_errors.inference: Treating a product or customer announcement as procurement
category_errors.why_not: An announcement names no delivered equipment, serial numbers or site

category_errors.inference: Treating a purchase order as delivery or installation
category_errors.why_not: An order records intent to buy; delivery and installation are separate records

chain.title: Physical installation
chain.question: What shows that racks were placed and connected to power, coolant and networks at a named site?

category_errors.inference: Treating a deployment guide as an installation record
category_errors.why_not: A guide states what an engineer should do; it records nothing done

chain.title: Commissioning
chain.question: What shows that a subsystem passed its commissioning tests?

category_errors.inference: Treating a published checklist as completed commissioning
category_errors.why_not: Unchecked items record what should be checked, not that anything was

category_errors.inference: Treating a test procedure as a passed test
category_errors.why_not: A procedure gives steps; a passed test needs results against criteria

chain.title: Acceptance
chain.question: What shows that the installed configuration, as a whole, met criteria the parties agreed?

category_errors.inference: Treating subsystem tests as whole-system acceptance
category_errors.why_not: Bring-up couples power, cooling, network and firmware; passing each alone does not show they work together

category_errors.inference: Treating a technical test as formal acceptance
category_errors.why_not: Acceptance is a signed decision against agreed criteria; a test supplies results, not the decision

category_errors.inference: Evaluating acceptance against criteria no public source defines
category_errors.why_not: The published checklist gives items without thresholds, so acceptance can only be judged against the parties' own criteria

chain.title: Operational observation
chain.question: What shows that the configuration operated under stated conditions over a stated period?

category_errors.inference: Treating a peak figure, a published test-suite description or a validated design as sustained operation
category_errors.why_not: None records a site, a period or measured results

category_errors.inference: Treating an installed software stack as performance
category_errors.why_not: Installed components show presence, not results

chain.title: Access and compliance
chain.question: Which documents bear on who may receive and use the configuration, separately from whether a site can run it?

category_errors.inference: Treating a 2024 announcement as the rule in force
category_errors.why_not: Only two current eCFR sections were reviewed

category_errors.inference: Treating rule text as a determination for a named transaction
category_errors.why_not: Controls attach to items, destinations, end uses and parties; a determination needs all of them

category_errors.inference: Treating access as a deployment stage that technical records complete
category_errors.why_not: Access is a separate dimension: technical records say nothing about who may receive the system

domains.claim: The named rack configuration is the one NVIDIA describes, and its trays are present
domains.acceptance_or_observation: Serial-numbered delivery and installation records for the named rack
domains.review_reason: Documentary comparison of serial numbers against the configuration; no engineering judgement

domains.claim: The site supplies and distributes the rack's power with the stated redundancy
domains.acceptance_or_observation: Energisation and load tests of the rack power path, with the redundancy scheme exercised
domains.review_reason: Redundancy and bus-bar capacity are open conflicts; judging a load test needs an electrical engineer

domains.claim: The facility removes the rack's heat through liquid and air within the stated envelope
domains.acceptance_or_observation: Coolant-loop commissioning and a thermal test under load with conditions and thresholds
domains.review_reason: No public coolant specification exists to test against; a mechanical engineer must set and judge the criteria

domains.claim: The NVLink domain and north-south network are brought up and integrated
domains.acceptance_or_observation: Bring-up logs showing the NVLink domain configured, and north-south switch installation and configuration records
domains.review_reason: Bring-up logs need a network engineer to read them against NVIDIA's sequence

domains.claim: The firmware and software baseline matches a stated, consistent version set, and validation ran
domains.acceptance_or_observation: A firmware and software inventory compared with the SBOM, and dated validation output
domains.review_reason: Version compatibility is not published; consistency must be judged by a specialist

domains.claim: The site operates the rack with leak response, artifact handling and a completed handover
domains.acceptance_or_observation: An integrated leak-response test, a signed acceptance record and monitoring over a stated period
domains.review_reason: Acceptance criteria are not public; whether monitoring evidence suffices is an engineering judgement

domains.claim: The parties may receive and use the configuration at the site
domains.acceptance_or_observation: A determination for the named transaction under the rules in force
domains.review_reason: A legal and compliance question, not an engineering one; no determination is made here

ide006_consistency.note: The cited passage is a procedural prerequisite (install the switches before deploying them), not a network design. Either the guide proposes a design, and its classification would be reference design, or the state is product specification documented. IDE-006 is not changed here; the question goes to editorial review.

matrix.claim: The rack configuration is 18 compute trays and 9 NVLink switch trays as NVIDIA describes
verification_conditions: Configuration identity matches the GB200 NVL72 description; GB200 and GB300 are kept apart
matrix.supported_inference: What the product is specified to contain
matrix.prohibited_inference: That any named rack contains it
matrix.gap: None at specification level; GB200 versus GB300 differences are open

matrix.claim: A scalable unit combines eight racks as the reference architecture proposes
verification_conditions: The tested-scale statement is read as written, with its ambiguity recorded
matrix.supported_inference: How NVIDIA proposes racks be combined and supplied
matrix.prohibited_inference: That any site built or tested a scalable unit
matrix.gap: Tested scale and the scalable-unit power remainder are unresolved

matrix.claim: The rack's power path provides the stated redundancy
verification_conditions: Redundancy scheme stated
Failover exercised under load
Results against criteria
matrix.supported_inference: That the redundancy scheme worked in a dated test
matrix.prohibited_inference: That redundancy is N+N or any scheme, from the conflicting public figures
matrix.gap: No commissioning record; the published scheme is itself in conflict

matrix.claim: The bus bar carries the rack's load on the stated paths
verification_conditions: Path count and rating stated
Load test with measured current per path
matrix.supported_inference: That the bus bar carried a stated load in a dated test
matrix.prohibited_inference: The path count, from arithmetic on the public rating
matrix.gap: No path count is published and no load test is public

matrix.claim: The facility meets the rack's coolant interface
verification_conditions: Coolant specification stated by NVIDIA or the parties
Loop commissioning results against it
matrix.supported_inference: That the coolant loop met a stated specification in a dated test
matrix.prohibited_inference: Any coolant requirement for GB200 NVL72, which no public source states
matrix.gap: No public coolant specification exists to commission against

matrix.claim: Firmware and software match a consistent, stated version set
verification_conditions: Inventory per rack and tray
Compared with the SBOM and NVIDIA's required versions
matrix.supported_inference: Which versions were installed on a named rack
matrix.prohibited_inference: That the versions are compatible, which NVIDIA does not publish as a set
matrix.gap: No public version set; the firmware guide was not reviewed

matrix.claim: The site has contracted and energised enough electrical capacity
verification_conditions: Utility agreement for the named site
Single-line diagram
Energisation results for the circuits serving the racks
matrix.supported_inference: That capacity was contracted for a named site
matrix.prohibited_inference: That contracted capacity was energised or is sufficient
matrix.stage_note: Workflow C places this under 'procured'; a utility capacity record is a site commitment, which the nine states record as capability contracted

matrix.claim: The configuration was delivered to a named site
verification_conditions: Delivery record with serial numbers matching the configuration
matrix.supported_inference: That named equipment reached a named site

matrix.claim: Racks are installed and connected at a named site
verification_conditions: Placement, power, coolant and network connections recorded
Every rack and connection covered
matrix.prohibited_inference: That any subsystem was energised or tested

matrix.claim: The NVLink domain and north-south network are brought up
verification_conditions: Bring-up log showing the NVLink domain configured before compute trays
North-south switch configuration records
matrix.supported_inference: That the network subsystems were brought up on a dated occasion
matrix.prohibited_inference: That the networks work together with compute under load

matrix.claim: Subsystems passed commissioning and validation tests
verification_conditions: Method, thresholds and results for each test
Dated, for the named configuration
matrix.supported_inference: That named subsystems passed stated tests
matrix.prohibited_inference: That the configuration as a whole was accepted
matrix.gap: No validation output is public; thresholds are not published

matrix.claim: The installed configuration was accepted against agreed criteria
verification_conditions: Criteria agreed before testing
Integrated test results
Signed by parties able to accept
matrix.supported_inference: That the parties accepted the configuration against stated criteria
matrix.prohibited_inference: That it met any public criterion, since none is published
matrix.gap: No acceptance record or criteria are public
matrix.stage_note: Workflow C places acceptance under 'commissioned'; acceptance presupposes an integrated test, so its earliest supportable state is integrated configuration verified

matrix.claim: The site monitored the configuration in operation over a stated period
verification_conditions: Observation period stated
Leak, power and thermal events recorded with the response
matrix.supported_inference: How the configuration behaved over the stated period
matrix.prohibited_inference: Behaviour outside that period or configuration
matrix.gap: No monitoring record is public; the building-management interface is not published

matrix.claim: The configuration delivered stated workload performance
verification_conditions: Workload, method, software versions and conditions stated
Repeatable by another party
matrix.supported_inference: Measured performance for the stated workload and conditions
matrix.prohibited_inference: Peak or vendor figures as delivered performance

matrix.claim: The parties may receive and use the configuration at the site
verification_conditions: Determination for the named items, parties, destination and end use, under the rules in force
matrix.supported_inference: How a named transaction is treated, once determined
matrix.prohibited_inference: Any determination from rule text alone
matrix.gap: Only two current eCFR sections and a 2024 announcement were reviewed; no determination exists

findings.text: No registered source supports a site-record claim, so every site-level state (contracted through operational observation) is not established from the reviewed public record for any GB200 NVL72 deployment.

The highest state any reviewed public source supports is infrastructure proposed, from NVIDIA's reference architecture. Under the record model, product documents and procedures reach product specification documented only; applied to the IDE-006 dossier, this flags one entry (req-nw-north-south) whose recorded state exceeds what its cited procedure can support, for editorial review.
Acceptance cannot be judged from public material even if site records were obtained: the published checklist names items without thresholds, so acceptance rests on criteria only the parties hold.

NVLink bring-up is the point where four domains meet: it needs power and coolant in place, a consistent firmware baseline, and it precedes cluster validation. A commissioning claim for the network is therefore not separable from electrical, thermal and software evidence.

Two Workflow C requirements sit in stages that differ from the record they need: site electrical capacity (rc-07) is a contracted commitment rather than a procurement, and acceptance (rc-12) presupposes an integrated test rather than subsystem commissioning.

review_questions.question: What load and failover tests should a commissioning record for a GB200 NVL72 rack power path contain to show the stated redundancy?
review_questions.why_it_matters: Redundancy figures conflict in public sources, so only a test record can show what a site has.
review_questions.would_settle: A test outline that a commissioning record can be checked against

review_questions.question: Without a published coolant specification, what must a liquid-loop commissioning record state for it to show the rack's cooling interface was met?
review_questions.why_it_matters: The thermal domain has no public criterion to commission against.
review_questions.would_settle: A minimum set of loop parameters and test conditions

review_questions.question: Which entries in an NVLink bring-up log show that the domain was configured as NVIDIA's sequence requires?
review_questions.why_it_matters: Bring-up is where power, cooling, firmware and network evidence meet.
review_questions.would_settle: The log fields a reviewer should look for

review_questions.question: How should a reviewer judge whether a rack's firmware and software inventory is a consistent set when NVIDIA does not publish one?
review_questions.why_it_matters: A version inventory shows what is installed, not whether it is compatible.
review_questions.would_settle: A method for checking consistency against NVIDIA's own documents

review_questions.question: What observation period and measurements would make an operational monitoring record for an AI rack meaningful?
review_questions.why_it_matters: Operational observation is the last state and the one most often claimed without records.
review_questions.would_settle: A minimum period and measurement set, with the reasoning

applications: Listing, before any claim about a named installation, which records must be requested and from whom
Checking whether a document offered as evidence can support the state claimed for it, or is a category error
Separating what a vendor documents from what a site has done, domain by domain
Identifying which domain's evidence a network or acceptance claim depends on
Keeping access and compliance questions apart from technical deployment evidence

public_reference_decision.reason: /ai-chip-infrastructure/ already publishes the nine evidence states with the record each needs, the seven-domain matrix and the GB200 NVL72 gaps. The typed record model here is unreviewed and largely refines that ladder, so it stays a research candidate until reviewed.
